rows.abstract: Provides for the following --- "SECTION 1. rows.abstract: Rationale: This bill seeks to put more impetus to the adoption of a rational national forest management policy that is geared towards giving upland communities and indigenous peoples management, rehabilitation, protection, enhancement and utilization of forest resources in a sustainable, well-planned and effecttive manner. Includes these vital provisions: (1) The creation of a CBFM Steering Committee tasked to prepare a national action plan and the policies, guidelines and strategies to implement such plan particularly such mechanisms for community and local government participation; (2) The creation of a CBFM Special Account to suport the implementation for the CBFM Action Plan; and (3) The institutionaliz ation of a training support assiistance program for participants in the CBFM.

rows.abstract: Rationale:"The Department of Transportation and Communication grappled with the different aspects of the traffic problem.  One of these, as being manifested in the LRT-3 project and inviting so much attentionm, was the commercial angle, which involved the real estate significance of the LRT projects, like the airspace over the lines and the areas in and around the stations. These income-earners of mammoth potentials were planned to be leased out by the developers." Declares it UNLAWFUL for anyperson, corporation or netity to construct or allow the construction of commercial or residential structurees above or below roads, bridges and transport systems, as well as stations thereof.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE ESTABLISHMENT OF THE PHILIPPINE EMERGENCY MEDICAL SERVICES SYSTEM AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Rationale: Preparedness is the key to minimizing or preventing the damaging effects of any emergency or disaster.  The organization and training of emergency response teams within the community is an important component of preparedness. This Act shall have the following objectives: (1) Organize volunteer emergency medical response teams in every municipality all over the country; (2) Train memebers of the emergency medical response teams on first aid, basic life support and other emergency procedures; (3) Establish a fully equipped and functional Medical Emergency and Disaster Management Operations and Coordinating Center to be known as Rescue 2000 Center to facilitate immediate and effective emergency response; and (4) Establish a networkk with all government and non -government organizations/g roups with emergency medical response capabilities.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 1996-08-15

rows.abstract: Rationale: During a period of calamity, epidemic, earthquake or national disaster, it is almost impossible ffor those responsible in the disbursement of public funds to adhere to the standard requirements authorized under the government auditing code, hence the proposed exemption. States that EXPENSE ACCOUNTS INCURRED DURING A PERIOD OF CALAMITY, EPIDEMIC, EARTHQUAKE OR NATIONAL DISASTER SHALL BE EXEMPT FROM THE ABOVE REQUIREMENTS AND/OR THE RIGID AUDITING PROCEDURES AND TECHNIQUES FOLLOWED INTHE EXAMINATION OF VOUCHERS AND OTHER DOCUMENTS; AND, PROVIDED, FURTHER. THAT EXPENSE ACOUNTS CHARGEABLE AGAINST LUMP-SUM APPROPRIATIONS, SUBJECT TO A SPECIAL BUDGET, SHALL BE AUDITED BASED ON THE APPROVED ITEMIZATION IN THE PSECIAL BUDGET, WHICH SHAALL SERVE AS THE AUTHORITY AND LEGAL BASIS.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING EMPLOYERS FROM REQUIRING JOB APPLICANTS TO PAY FEES OR BUY OR SELL PRODUCTS, AND PRESCRIBING PENALTIES THEREOF
rows.abstract: Rationale: Employment is a problem that badly affects our countryment, that they are willing to do anything to land a decent job.  Many of those who apply have fallen prey to the unscrupulous ways of ilelgal recruiters. Our desperate countrymen sometimes pay a high placement fee sourced from their life savings or even from loans or proceeds of the sale of their homes only to find disappointment after they are sent abroad without the promised job or after the recruiter absconds with their money.Declares it UNLAWFUL for anyone offering employment to require job applicants to do the following: (1) Pay fees to defray the cost of seminars, processing, examiantions or any similar expense. (2) Sell products without receiving the regular commissiion. (3) Buy products of the employer.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 1996-08-20

rows.title_full: THE SOLAR CONVERSION POWER SYSTEMS ACT OF 1996
rows.abstract: Aims to --- (1) Facilitate and accelerate the intorudction, development and local manufacture of advanced technology state-of-the-ar t solar conversion power systems; (2) Drastically reduce to a minimum the cost of building and maintaining large solar-oeprated power systems; and (3) Make available the wide-scale use in the country of cost-effective and reliable solar energy by homeowners, schools, hospitals, business, industry and agriculture. Directs the Dept. of Energy to design a program that will implement the objectives of this measure; contains provisions on other areas of concern, such as: (1) Exemptions and benefits for participating in the Program; and (2) Guidelines in formulating the Program.

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO ACHIEVE SELF-RELIANCE IN THE COUNTRY'S ENERGY REQUIREMENTS THROUGH THE EXPLOITATION OF NON-CONVENTIONA L ENERGY RESOURCES SUCH AS, BUT NOT LIMITED TO, BIOMASS, SOLAR, WIND, MICROHYDRO AND OCEAN ENERGY, PROVIDING INCENTIVES FOR DEVELOPERS,MANUFACTURERS AND USERS OF NON-CONVENTIONA L ENERGY SYSTEMS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Most nonconventional energy systems are environment-saf e, as in wind andd solar energy systems, andd even environment-enh anccing, as in systems for recycling waste into gas and biomass. Isolated groups and individuals have persisted andtriumphed in their efforts to harness nonconventional sources of energy for daily home and indsutrial use.  The Philippines is not lacking in such forward-looking and enterprising citizens, who have sometimes deplored the perceived lack of genuine government interest in their work." "National Nonconvetional Energy Program Act of 1996" Refers to energy systems which use renewable energy resources applying new energy conversion or utilizing innovative techniques. These systems can be characterizeed as indigenous small-scale, decentralized andd modular.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ENERGY since 1996-08-26
